standard.title: Develop ideas with connectives
standard.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts whose purposes may be imaginative, informative and persuasive, developing ideas using visual features, text structure appropriate to the topic and purpose, text connectives, expanded noun groups, specialist and technical vocabulary, and punctuation including dialogue punctuation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts with complex sentences, expanded noun groups, specialist vocabulary, and dialogue punctuation (AC9E4LY06). They have not yet deliberately developed ideas using text connectives and visual features in combination, or applied these tools across all three text type purposes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts across imaginative, informative and persuasive purposes, deliberately developing ideas using text connectives, expanded noun groups, specialist vocabulary, appropriate text structure, and accurate punctuation including dialogue.

nodes.label: Planning for purpose and structure
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select an appropriate text structure for their writing purpose and plan how content will be sequenced and grouped within that structure.
nodes.minimum_width: For a writing task, identify the text type and its structure, and plan how their content will be organised — including how the topic will be introduced, how information will be grouped, and how the text will conclude.
nodes.typical_width: Select appropriate text structure for purpose and audience, and plan content sequencing including: introduction of topic, grouping of related information in well-sequenced paragraphs, and a concluding statement. Use planning to organise information gathered from research or experience before drafting.
wider: Compare planning approaches across different text type purposes (imaginative, informative, persuasive) — examining how the planning tools (narrative map, argument plan, information organiser) differ and why
Plan a multimodal text and decide how visual and written elements will be distributed across the text structure, explaining the distribution rationale
success_criteria: Produces a plan that reflects the correct text structure for the purpose and sequences content logically within it.
The plan distinguishes between introduction, body structure, and conclusion — not just a list of points.

nodes.label: Developing ideas through language choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop ideas in their writing using text connectives, expanded noun groups, and specialist vocabulary, making deliberate choices about how these tools contribute to the text's development.
nodes.minimum_width: In a draft text, identify and explain at least two deliberate language choices — text connectives, expanded noun groups, or specialist vocabulary — and explain how each develops an idea or serves the text's purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Draft a text that demonstrates deliberate use of text connectives (to signal relationship and sequence), expanded noun groups (for precision and description), and specialist vocabulary (for technical accuracy and register). Explain the function of each type of language choice in developing the text's ideas.
wider: Examine how text connective choices differ across text type purposes — comparing how connectives in narrative (sequence, time), argument (concession, causation), and explanation (cause, condition) serve different ideational purposes
Apply specialist and technical vocabulary appropriate to a specific learning area in an informative text, and compare the precision achieved with and without specialist terms
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 4 requires students to edit for meaning, structure, and accuracy — including reviewing their connective choices, noun groups, and vocabulary for precision. Students who have not yet made deliberate language choices in drafting have nothing substantive to edit at the craft level; their editing will default to surface-level fixes rather than the meaning-development work Node 4 demands.

response_modes.reason: Students often use text connectives as sentence-starters rather than as tools that signal the logical relationship between ideas. Encountering connective choices across argument, explanation, narrative, and informative writing contexts helps students see that connective selection is a meaning choice, not a formula.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The combination of text connective choices, expanded noun groups, and specialist vocabulary as a unified toolkit for developing ideas across text type purposes is genuinely rich. Advancing students can develop a cross-purpose grammar of how these tools function differently in imaginative, informative, and persuasive writing.
success_criteria: Uses text connectives to signal the logical relationship between ideas — not just as sentence openers.
Uses at least one expanded noun group and one specialist vocabulary choice and can explain the function of each in context.

nodes.label: Visual features in multimodal texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and create multimodal texts that use visual features deliberately to develop ideas alongside written language.
nodes.minimum_width: Create or annotate a multimodal text identifying at least two visual features and explaining how each contributes to the text's development of ideas or purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and create a multimodal text in which visual features (images, layout, diagrams, typography) are selected and positioned deliberately to develop ideas alongside written language. Explain how the visual and written elements work together.
wider: Compare how visual features serve different purposes in imaginative versus informative multimodal texts — discussing how layout, image choice, and design conventions differ across text type purposes
Examine how digital composition tools affect visual feature choices and discuss how the medium shapes what is possible and expected
success_criteria: Includes visual features in a multimodal text and explains how they develop ideas or serve the text's purpose — not just decorates.
Demonstrates that visual feature placement or choice was deliberate, not incidental.

nodes.label: Editing for structure, meaning and accuracy
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit their own and others' texts for precision in text structure, meaning, grammar, spelling and punctuation including dialogue punctuation.
nodes.minimum_width: Review a draft and make at least three targeted editing changes — at least one addressing text structure or meaning and at least one addressing grammatical accuracy or punctuation (including dialogue punctuation if present).
nodes.typical_width: Re-read and edit texts using negotiated criteria covering text structure and meaning accuracy, and grammar, spelling and punctuation including dialogue punctuation. Apply digital tools where appropriate for surface-level editing. Distinguish between editing for meaning/structure and editing for accuracy.
wider: Exchange texts with a peer and apply editing criteria collaboratively, discussing the feedback given and received and what criteria-based editing reveals about the text
Create a personal editing checklist based on recurring patterns in their own writing — developing metacognitive awareness of individual writing strengths and challenges

response_modes.reason: Editing requires students to apply planning knowledge (node 1), language choice knowledge (node 2), and visual feature knowledge (node 3) simultaneously to evaluate and improve a draft — the full Phase D demand of the capability cycle.

success_criteria: Makes at least three targeted editing changes addressing different editing dimensions (structure/meaning AND accuracy/punctuation).
Uses dialogue punctuation correctly in texts where dialogue appears.
